rules.name: Generic scene-setting opening
rules.description: Broad openings delay the first useful fact and can fit almost any topic.
rules.message: The text opens with reusable scene-setting rather than the actual subject.
rules.suggestion: Start with the decision, event, example, or claim that made the text necessary.

patterns: (?:^|\n\s*\n)\s*(?:in today(?:'s)? (?:fast-paced|digital|modern) world|in the modern world|nowadays\b|in an era of\b|as the world becomes increasingly\b)

rules.name: Not-just contrast
rules.description: The formula `not just X, but Y` often inflates a straightforward claim.
rules.message: A stock contrast is carrying emphasis instead of evidence.
rules.suggestion: State the concrete effect directly, unless the contrast is genuinely necessary.

rules.name: Announced transition
rules.description: The writer announces that a topic will be explored instead of beginning the topic.
rules.message: The sentence previews the next section without adding content.
rules.suggestion: Delete the announcement and begin with the first substantive sentence.

patterns: \blet(?:'s| us) (?:dive in|dive into|delve into|explore|take a closer look)\b

rules.name: Formulaic conclusion
rules.description: Stock conclusion labels often repeat a point the reader already understood.
rules.message: The paragraph announces that it is a conclusion.
rules.suggestion: End on the strongest fact, decision, or unresolved consequence instead.

patterns: \b(?:in conclusion|to sum up|in summary|all in all)\b

rules.name: Fake-candid framing
rules.description: Self-labeling a sentence as honest does not make it more credible.
rules.message: The text announces candor instead of earning it through specifics.
rules.suggestion: Remove the framing and state the point directly.

patterns: \b(?:let(?:'s| us) be honest|the truth is|honestly\?|here(?:'s| is) the honest truth)\b

rules.name: Question with a canned short answer
rules.description: A tiny question-answer pair can imitate conversational rhythm without real dialogue.
rules.message: The question is answered with a canned fragment.
rules.suggestion: Use a real question with a developed answer, or turn both into one statement.
